subject: PeakCommerce — goodwill package proposal after 2026-07-11 outage
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@peakcommerce.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-11 09:18 PDT
Subject: Major slowdown + 503s during 07/11 nightly batch — request for remediation and credits

Hi Redwood team,

We saw a significant degradation in API responsiveness last night (around 01:10–02:30 PT) that affected our order enrichment pipeline. Symptoms: elevated 5xx rate (peaked ~18%), long tail latencies (p95 jumped from 250ms to ~2.8s), and several timed-out jobs that had to be retried. This cost us a few hours of processing and pushed orders into a delayed state for customers.

We need:
- A concise timeline of what you observed and root-cause (we need this for our outage RCA)
- Confirmation of any SLA credits or goodwill you can offer — our procurement asks that compensation be credited to our account or applied toward our committed capacity for July/August
- Short-term mitigation steps/patch ETA if there are any remaining risks

Please loop in whoever owns escalations — we are sensitive about this because it impacted peak settlement windows.

Thanks,
Rajesh Kumar
VP Engineering, PeakCommerce
rajesh@peakcommerce.com
ops@peakcommerce.com

[Attachment: peak-nightly-errors.log (text/attachments-stub)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-11 10:02 PDT
Subject: Fwd: Major slowdown + 503s during 07/11 nightly batch — request for remediation and credits

Team — forwarding Rajesh's note. Quick summary from our side: ops saw a spike in queueing during a node drain window; a KV cache invalidation path retried and amplified latency under load. Dylan is running the timeline and root-cause now.

Proposed initial goodwill package (for internal approval):
- USD 12,000 of service credits applied to PeakCommerce account (to be used against hosted usage)
- 45-day trial/extension on their onboarding sandbox so their migration window isn't impacted
- Waive July overage charges related to the incident window
- Offer a priority onboarding slot and two hours of dedicated onboarding time with our SREs

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (draft) — will update with timestamps from infra.

Asks: Sean/Monica — can you approve the credits and trial extension? Legal procurement usually requires a written offer doc (see link below) — if approved, I'll send the formal proposal to Rajesh and the procurement mailbox.

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (csv/attachments-stub)]

Approve credits amount and trial extension as suggested. Monica, can you draft the external language? I’ll be on standby for sign-off.

—Sean

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11 11:05 PDT
Subject: internal: incident timeline and ops notes for PeakCommerce 07/11
To: oncall@redwood.com

Team — short summary pulled from tracing and autoscaler logs:
- 01:07 PT: control-plane started rolling a drain for a maintenance patch across a subset of nodes (unfortunate overlap with high-volume batch window)
- 01:10–01:20 PT: KV cache invalidation path triggered retries; increased CPU on replica set B
- 01:20–02:10 PT: elevated tail latency and transient 502/503s while requests retried across failing backends
- 02:15 PT: autoscaler stabilized and drain completed; normal latencies resumed by ~02:30 PT

Root cause: scheduling window + an uncaught retry amplification path on cache miss during draining. Remediation: change drain to cordon/stream-drain, add backoff on KV invalidation retries, and tighten drain scheduling. Proposed mitigations deployed to canary today — monitoring looks good.

I attached an SLA usage snapshot and the CSV timeline. Happy to jump on a quick call with Peak if they want a more detailed RCA.

Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: sla-usage-snapshot.png, incident-timeline.csv]
